SMTO-CMP-0041 — Fast Cache couldn't be loaded or changed right now

GUID: b093b804-256d-4109-a0d8-eebf03ad5344
Slug: cache-management-unavailable
Domain: CMP · Subsystem: cmp

What happened

  • SMTO couldn't open or change its Fast Cache, the saved shortcuts it uses to repeat exact prompts faster. Your conversations and task results aren't affected; only managing these shortcuts failed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Settings › Agent behavior › Fast Cache and select Refresh. This reads the Fast Cache again, which works if the problem was brief.
  2. If you were pinning or removing a prompt, check the list to see whether that change already took effect before trying it again. The change may have gone through even though SMTO showed an error.
  3. If the list still won't load, ask the person who manages SMTO to check that SMTO can read and write its data folder and has free disk space. Once that's fixed, it's safe to select Refresh again. Fast Cache is kept in a file in SMTO's data folder, so it can't load when that file can't be opened.

What success looks like

  • The Fast Cache section shows the Pinned and Learned counts and lists your pinned prompts.

If it still fails

  • Open Technical details, select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't select Clear learned or delete files in SMTO's data folder to make the error go away; that removes saved data without fixing the cause.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A Fast Cache management operation failed because the verified execution cache store could not be accessed (legacy cache_management_unavailable identity; current routes report cache_unavailable).

What this means

  • The retained cache_management_unavailable identity describes explicit cache-management access failure, but no current direct producer was found in the reviewed source. Completion checks consume retained evidence and the effective guard policy; they do not execute work. A rejected declaration preserves the answer and successful receipts, and only the original operation evidence establishes effects.

Why this can happen

  • The retained cache_management_unavailable identity describes explicit cache-management access failure, but no current direct producer was found in the reviewed source.

How to diagnose it

  • Locate the original emitting component and cache access condition while keeping authoritative receipts separate.

How to fix it

  • Check the Server log for the exception behind the failing /api/agent/fast-cache request and confirm that verified_execution_cache.db, beside the run store in the agent state directory, is readable and writable. Repair only that store access; do not delete cache or run data, and do not treat this as a task failure because task receipts are stored separately.
  • Inspect the original cache-management diagnostic and repair only its supported store access; preserve authoritative task receipts.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • Supported cache management works or the actual component defect is reported without rebuilding task effects.

What not to do

  • Do not remove retained state or weaken trust checks to make an unavailable dependency appear healthy.

Technical notes

  • Completion checks consume retained evidence and the effective guard policy; they do not execute work. A rejected declaration preserves the answer and successful receipts, and only the original operation evidence establishes effects.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
